newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bosnia, Croatia pledge to further co-operation.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia, Croatia pledge to further co-operation.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Bosnia's presidency chairman Alija Izetbegovic reaffirmed at a summit on Wednesday the right of all refugees in Bosnia to return home in safety without intimidation.

They also pledged to strengthen the political independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina and said they would draw up an agreement outlining relations between the two countries which would "further co-operation", they said in a joint statement.

"The right of refugees to an organised, voluntary and safe return to their homes, with protection from intimidation and the establishment of the necessary legal framework was reaffirmed," said the statement, issued after talks in Split.

It came days after hundreds of Moslem refugees fled their homes under intimidation from angry, drunken Croats in central Bosnia. They had returned to their pre-war homes over the past three weeks and vowed to return again.

"I think we had overestimated the possibility of implementing something like the return of refugees, freedom of movement and punishment of war criminals. We have overestimated the pace at which it can go, but recently there have been some positive trends," Izetbegovic told reporters.
The statement said the two countries would exchange draft agreements on bilateral relations by September 1.
